assessment.security_status_en: The security situation in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz remains critical due to escalating Houthi attacks and Iranian operations that are paralyzing key maritime trade routes. Reports of sunken container ships, targeted tankers, and disrupted oil supplies are driving massive risk premiums and global shipping disruptions.

recommendations.reason_cs: Přetrvávající krize v Hormuzském průlivu a Rudém moři prodlužuje trasy a žene spotové sazby za přepravu prudce nahoru. To generuje nadstandardní příjmy pro provozovatele kontejnerových flotil a tankerů.
recommendations.reason_en: The ongoing crisis in the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea extends shipping routes and drives spot freight rates sharply higher. This generates exceptional revenues for container and tanker fleet operators.

recommendations.reason_en: Brent crude topping $110 per barrel due to the Persian Gulf blockade and attacks on tankers delivers enormous margins and strong cash flow growth for energy majors.

recommendations.reason_en: Rising maritime shipping costs, extended delivery routes around Africa, and inflationary pressures from expensive energy heavily weigh on manufacturing margins and European consumer demand.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called US President Donald Trump “by far, the greatest friend Israel has ever had”, in footage he shared a day after Trump endorsed him ahead of Israel’s upcoming elections.

articles.title: Trump says Nato 'weren't there to help' during war on Iran
articles.summary:
Trump says Nato 'weren't there to help' during war on Iran

US President Donald Trump has slammed Nato allies, saying they "weren't there to help" Washington during its war on Iran. 

"We stand with Europe despite its flaws, its weaknesses…But if they don't soon find their way, and they have to find their way, we will have no choice but to leave," he said at a campaign rally.

"We spend hundreds of billions of dollars a year on Nato protecting them, but when we said, 'Would you like to help?' 'No, thank you.' 'Oh, no thank you?' What does that mean, 'No, thank you'?"

Trump added that the US spent "so much money on Nato", adding that they "weren't there to help" and that its something Washington "can never really forget".

articles.title: Houthi attack kills 53 in biggest single loss of life since Yemen civil war reignited
articles.summary:
More than 200 mostly young people said to be injured after ballistic missile attack on training camp for government forces

At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government security forces, making it the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September.

The attack on al-Alam camp in the southern Shabwa province was said to have injured more than 200 others, mostly young recruits, and was described as a disaster by the country’s UN-recognised government. The injured were taken from the police and army training camp in the Jardan district to a hospital in the local capital, Ataq, where pleas for blood donations were made.

articles.title: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina
articles.summary:
Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next

A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn.

Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors peered down on the scene.

Húthiské útoky a námořní miny ochromují klíčové obchodní trasy a nutí mocnosti k přímým vojenským blokádám.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea is reaching a critical tipping point due to escalating attacks on oil supertankers, merchant vessels, and government infrastructure in Yemen. Houthi strikes and naval mines are crippling key trade routes and forcing powers into direct military blockades.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further escalation of attacks in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea is expected, keeping oil prices and maritime freight rates at extreme highs.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Rudého moře, Adenského zálivu a Hormuzského průlivu zůstává kritická kvůli pokračujícím útokům Houthiů na ropné tankery a infrastrukturu (včetně úderů v Saúdské Arábii). archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, and Strait of Hormuz remains critical due to ongoing Houthi attacks on oil tankers and infrastructure, including strikes in Saudi Arabia. Konflikt se rozšiřuje, přičemž incidenty jako potopení kontejnerové lodi a útoky na ropnou infrastrukturu udržují vysokou nervozitu na trzích.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf remains critical due to ongoing attacks on tankers and merchant vessels.
